clue.text: Skipped along dressed like Ridinghood?

blocks.note: first meaning: danced or frisked along playfully
second meaning: wearing a red cape, as Little Red Riding Hood did

explanation.surface: A girl skips along through the woods dressed as Little Red Riding Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: read the answer as CAPE-RED, the way Red Riding Hood went about, in her scarlet hooded cape.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap or frolic about, so a skipping gait is a caper in the past tense.

clue.text: “When the — 's finished jumping on his mother” (Gilbert)

definitions.text: “When the — 's finished jumping on his mother” (Gilbert)

blocks.clueFragment: “When the — 's finished jumping on his mother”
blocks.note: surface reading: a startling line about someone stamping on a parent
setter's reading: fill the gap from the policemen's song in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Pirates of Penzance

explanation.walkthrough: The line runs 'When the coster's finished jumping on his mother, He loves to lie a-basking in the sun'. A coster, short for costermonger, is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Gilbert's lyric is the street hawker, a London barrow trader of fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: Colonnade and gateway I take care of

blocks.note: a port is a gate or gateway, as in the old city gates
taken as written
c/o, 'care of', the address abbreviation

explanation.surface: A building's entrance has a colonnade and gateway that the speaker looks after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care of' looks like a verb phrase; it is c/o, as written on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch supported on columns, a short row of pillars before a building's entrance.

clue.text: Figure in recipe halved to produce confusion

indicators.note: cutting something in half means only its first three of six letters stay

blocks.note: taken as written, before it is cut down
a tangle is a muddle or confused state

explanation.surface: Cutting a recipe in half leaves the cook confused about the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a number in the recipe; it is a geometric shape. Half of RECIPE is REC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is a four-sided geometric shape with right angles, one example of a plane figure.

clue.text: Meet your don to rewrite book

indicators.note: rewriting something sets it down again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student is told to meet their tutor in order to rewrite a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like the student's essay; it is a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuteronomy is the fifth book of the Old Testament, the last of the five books of Moses.

clue.text: Packed suit into last stage

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the second

blocks.note: the end is the final stage
a lawsuit is a case in court

explanation.surface: Someone packs their suit at the last stage of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing being packed; it is a legal suit, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something encased is enclosed in a covering or box, which is what a packed item is.

clue.text: Direction followed by the old seer

blocks.note: E is east, a compass direction
ye is the archaic spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A prophet of old gives directions, followed by his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' looks like a prophet; read literally, it is one who sees.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye is the organ that sees, so it is literally a seer, a pun on the prophet sense.

clue.text: Many a month - well, not quite - in the island

indicators.note: something not quite complete falls just short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
one month of the year, before it is cut short

explanation.surface: Many a month is spent, or nearly, on holiday on the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many a month' reads as one phrase; it splits into a numeral and a month.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is the well-known Italian island in the Bay of Naples, a holiday resort.

clue.text: Russian town girl with empty box?

blocks.note: a girl's name
the box is slang for television
empty means holding nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl in a Russian town is handed an empty box.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the television, and making it empty puts O, nothing, inside it. Saratov is a city on the Volga.
explanation.definitionFit: Saratov is a large city on the Volga in south-western Russia, so a Russian town.

clue.text: They help in more than one sort of theatre

definitions.text: They help in more than one sort of theatre

blocks.clueFragment: They help in more than one sort of theatre
blocks.note: surface reading: stagehands working for several kinds of drama

blocks.clueFragment: more than one sort of theatre
blocks.note: setter's reading: both a playhouse, where they clothe actors, and an operating theatre, where they once bandaged patients

explanation.walkthrough: In a playhouse they help actors into costume; in old hospitals they were surgeons' assistants who changed wound dressings in the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names assistants who clothe stage actors and also, historically, surgical helpers who bandaged wounds.

clue.text: Criticism of wrecked cruiser - that's heartless

the outside letters of that, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A ship's crew take criticism over a wrecked cruiser, and call the critic heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes CRUISER plus TT from the ends of that.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a piece of severe criticism or censure, as in strictures on someone's conduct.

clue.text: Simple – e's in the soup, perhaps

blocks.note: pure in the sense of plain, unmixed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook notes that a simple dish has an e in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E's in' means the letter E is added on. 'Perhaps' flags that soup is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is food blended smooth, and a thick soup is one example of such a dish.

clue.text: Revitalized part is title role

indicators.note: only a part of the word is wanted, a run of letters lying inside it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: An actor's revitalized career rests on landing a title role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a stage role, matching the surface; it signals a part of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón is the heroine of the Lloyd Webber musical Evita, so her nickname is the show's name and lead character.

clue.text: Waste time with a case, foolishly

definitions.note: the answer is the third-person form, 'wastes'; the definition is the bare verb

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer foolishly wastes time on a hopeless case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste time' reads as one idiom; 'Waste' alone is the definition, in the sense of wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make thin and wasted, so it matches waste in the sense of grow or make gaunt.

clue.text: Cancel calls about article giving elder's age

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word wraps around the small word

blocks.note: to annul is to cancel or make void
a is the indefinite article
rings as in telephone calls

explanation.surface: Someone cancels phone calls about an item announcing a senior relative's age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elder' looks like an older person; it is the elder tree, whose age its growth rings show.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth rings in a trunk's cross-section, one laid down each year, reveal how old a tree is.

clue.text: Argentine pirate? Give full name

blocks.note: surface reading: a buccaneer from Argentina
setter's reading: argentine means silvery, so the pirate is the one surnamed for that metal; the clue asks for his name in full

explanation.walkthrough: Argent is the heraldic word for silver, and argentine means silvery. The pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island is called Silver, and the instruction asks for all three of his names.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's one-legged buccaneer in Treasure Island bears the metal's name as surname, preceded by his two nicknames.

clue.text: Fish product subject to conditions arising on vessel

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading from the bottom up, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: nisi is the legal term for a conditional order, as in decree nisi
a glass is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A fish product is sold only on conditions printed on its jar.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree nisi is a court order that becomes final unless conditions intervene; nisi is Latin for unless.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin obtained from the swim bladders of sturgeon and other fish.

clue.text: A rebel prophet, briefly meeting scholar

blocks.note: taken as written
Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450
Mic. is the short form of Micah, the Old Testament prophet and book

explanation.surface: A rebel and a prophet hold a short meeting with a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade is the stock crossword rebel; 'briefly' points to the Bible's abbreviation for Micah.
explanation.definitionFit: An academic is a university teacher or researcher, a person devoted to learning and study.

clue.text: Like French speeches around many Oxford festivals

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so the two words wrap the letter for many

blocks.note: comme is French for like
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a stand-in for many
orations are formal speeches

explanation.surface: Speakers at Oxford's festivals deliver their speeches in a French manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Commemoration, Commem for short, is Oxford University's summer ceremony honouring benefactors, with its Commem balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Commemoration is Oxford University's annual celebration of founders and benefactors, held each summer with balls.

clue.text: Cosmetic many found as dear in Italy

blocks.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a stand-in for many
taken as written
cara is Italian for dear

explanation.surface: Many people find cosmetics expensive in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like expensive; it is the term of endearment, put into Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic painted on the eyelashes to darken and thicken them.

clue.text: It would be odd if it was never in neurologist's prescription

indicators.note: something odd is out of the ordinary, so these letters appear in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It would be strange if a nerve specialist never prescribed this.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that calms or strengthens the nerves, the kind a nerve doctor might prescribe.

clue.text: Spare journalist was so inclined

blocks.note: spare and lean both mean thin
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A thin journalist felt so inclined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So inclined' looks like willing; it means tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean is to slope or tilt to one side, so the past tense means was at an angle.

clue.text: HMS Siva?

blocks.note: surface reading: the name of a Royal Navy ship
setter's reading: Siva, or Shiva, is the Hindu god of destruction, and a naval vessel named for him would be a warship of that class

explanation.walkthrough: In Hindu belief Siva is the Destroyer within the trinity with Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver; HMS shows we want a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is both a fast naval warship class and the title of the Hindu god of dissolution.

clue.text: Soldier's radio - correct type?

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, so the soldiers
a radio is a wireless set

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like model; it is printer's type, which is set and, to correct it, set again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset type is to compose it again in printing, the way a compositor fixes an error.

clue.text: One or two notes produced in the throat

two musical notes, G and E

explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two notes' reads as a handful; split it into one note, or, two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorge is an old word for the throat or gullet, still heard in 'my gorge rises'.

clue.text: Intends to take no extreme measures

explanation.surface: Someone plans to avoid taking extreme measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme measures' reads as drastic action; here measures are statistical values, and averages lie between the extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to intend, and the plural noun is the averages of statistics, central values between highs and lows.

clue.text: Public excitement? One isn't as funny as all that

clue.text: One gets this first in order to rise

clue.text: America's turn to make payment - or fail thus to do so?

blocks.note: US, the United States

explanation.surface: America takes its turn to pay, or fails to pay, at a summit.
